2296ec38aa1d645d: SEPANG: Hakim Danish Ramli put recent struggles behind him by qualifying third for the Petronas Grand Prix of Malaysia at the Sepang International Circuit today.
His performance earned Malaysia's first front-row start in the lightweight class at Sepang since his mentor and manager, Zulfahmi Khairuddin, clinched pole in 2012.
"I had been struggling for a number of rounds before the Malaysian GP, I was at the back," said the Aeon Credit-MT Helmets-MSI rider.
"I was worried before the start of my own home GP (due to expectations). But I never let that break my spirit.
"I tried my best to think positive and was determined to give it my best this week.
"Starting from the front is really important if I want to stay with the fast riders. I will try to fight with them until the end."
Danish clocked two minutes 10.529 seconds to take third place (+0.133s) in the second qualifying session (Q2).
World champion Maximo Quiles (CFMoto Gaviota Aspar) clinched pole in 2:10.396s, while Red Bull KTM Ajo's Brian Uriarte was second (+0.084s).
Danish produced strong results earlier this season, finishing third at Mugello and securing his maiden grand prix win at Brno, both in July.
That victory made him the first Malaysian to win a Moto3 race since Khairul Idham Pawi in 2016.
However, Danish's form dipped after the summer break, managing only two top-10 finishes since Brno, the most recent at the Red Bull Ring four rounds ago.
3a5076f1991ba0f7: KUANTAN: Two men were arrested on suspicion of processing ketum juice at a house in Jaya Gading here yesterday.
The General Operations Force (GOF) seized 540 packets of ketum juice and three sacks containing ketum leaves during a raid at 2pm.
GOF Southeast Brigade commander Senior Assistant Commissioner Datuk Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the raid was conducted under Op Taring Mitra after a team monitored the premises.
"The team spotted a Proton Saga entering the house before moving in to conduct checks when two men got out of the vehicle.
"Checks led to the discovery of 540 packets of ketum juice and three sacks containing about 33kg of ketum leaves, with an estimated total value of RM17,520," he said in a statement today.
He said the team also seized several kitchen appliances, including a gas cylinder and pots believed to have been used to boil the ketum leaves.
"Investigations revealed that both suspects obtained ketum leaves from outside Pahang and used the house to process the juice before selling it," he said.
He said the case was being investigated under Section 30(3) of the Poisons Act 1952, which provides for a maximum fine of RM100,000, jail of up to five years, or both, upon conviction.

99cf1dd98841fa40: MELAKA, Oct 31 — Pakatan Harapan has dismissed suggestions that it engineered the Registrar of Societies’ move to suspend Perikatan Nasional, insisting the matter stems from troubles inside the opposition bloc.

Melaka PKR chief Adam Adli Abd Halim rejected the allegation outright and pushed back against Gerakan president Datuk Dr Dominic Lau’s assertion that the suspension carried a political motive, the New Straits Times reported.
“We reject these allegations. This has nothing to do with us. It is not our strategy, and we are not involved at all,” he said at a press conference at the PH main operations centre.
“That is their internal conflict,” he added.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail and Bentong MP Young Syefura Othman were also present.
Adam said that PH’s priority was a fair electoral contest that lets Melaka voters choose their next state government.
“We have made it clear that the election in Melaka is a democratic process to give voters the opportunity to decide who should form the state government,” he said.
“It has nothing to do with any disputes or political disagreements unrelated to the electoral process.”
Lau had alleged on Thursday that the RoS action formed part of a PH strategy ahead of the Melaka polls.
“Why was PN suspended only now? This is a malicious intent. This is a political decision, this is indeed PH’s agenda,” he was quoted as saying at PN’s candidate announcement event.
Lau further claimed the suspension was meant to ease Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s path to a second term, tying it to PKR’s Melaka congress on Aug 16.
PN secured reprieve on Oct 22 when the High Court stayed the RoS decision to revoke its registration, pending its judicial review application.
The court also halted enforcement of an RoS notice suspending PN’s activities, clearing the coalition to keep operating and to contest the Melaka election.
Adam said PH would spend the campaign promoting its candidates and policies.
He added that the coalition would shun personal attacks and divisive tactics, especially those aimed at younger candidates.
Polling for the Melaka election is set for Nov 14, with early voting on Nov 10.
cdca307476760a29: KUALA LUMPUR, October 31 — The stage is almost set for the return of Malaysia’s highly acclaimed theatre production Puteri Gunung Ledang The Musical (PGL).
Seventeen years since its last full theatrical run, PGL will once again mesmerise audiences from October 31 to November 15 with 19 shows scheduled for the 15-day run.

Adding to its appeal this time around, the musical will depart from its flagship home at Istana Budaya to take up residency at the newly opened, state-of-the-art Jeffrey Cheah Performing Arts Centre (JCPAC) Grand Theatre in Sunway Square.

Despite the leap into modern projection mapping, immersive soundscapes, and advanced stagecraft, director Puan Sri Tiara Jacquelina is adamant about one principle: technology will never override the human core of the story.
“We used to be low-tech and people already loved it and this time, with new technology, we want to see how much further we can elevate PGL but we will never, ever let technology lead.
“If audiences walk out talking only about lights and projections, we’ve failed. For me, the acting and storytelling must come first,” Tiara said.

That commitment to storytelling is felt across every layer of the 2026 staging—from its 50-strong ensemble, where every single member has been assigned a specific name, backstory, and social stance within the Melaka court, down to its newly minted lead cast charged with honoring an iconic legacy.
The weight of legacy
**NP_IMAGE_BODY[371576]**<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Actor and competitive jujitsu athlete Mila Mohsin sees Gusti Puteri as a huge feminist icon. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
At the center of this revival is the formidable role of Gusti Puteri Retno Dumilah, famously originated by Tiara herself.
For actor and competitive jujitsu athlete Mila Mohsin, stepping into her mother’s footsteps carries both immense weight and a profound sense of purpose.
“It’s never easy doing reruns where the character was previously defined by one person—what more when it’s your own mother,” Mila shares candidly.
“Of course I feel the pressure, but I believe pressure makes diamonds.
“From young, I’ve always leaned into challenges. I want to be pushed to grow as an artist and as a person.”
To portray the Javanese princess, Mila spent time in Solo, Indonesia, along with some other cast and creative team, immersing themselves in ancient tata krama (royal customs) and Javanese philosophy.
Dissecting the character through a psychological lens rather than treating her as a mere folklore figure, Mila views Gusti Puteri through a distinctly modern framework.
“To me, Gusti Puteri is a huge feminist icon.
“She isn’t just a dancer or a young girl chasing romance—she is fighting for her freedom. That is her ultimate struggle, and that is where I connect with her most,” Mila said.
Mila approaches the physical demands of the role not through conventional musical dance, but as an embodied athletic and spiritual practice.
Working under Javanese master Mak Galo, she learned to lower her center of gravity to align with traditional Javanese posture (doyok).
“Javanese movement is about being closer to the earth—everything is lower, more humble, and set to a slower frequency.
“It’s not standard dance; it’s like a practice blending martial elements and yoga. As Mak Galo told us: ‘Sakitnya harus dinikmati’—you have to enjoy the painful process,” she said.

She also draws a strict distinction between off-stage identity and performance, focusing exclusively on how Gusti Puteri would authentically think and act rather than imitating her mother’s established stage habits or relying on her own personality.
Two visionaries, one princess
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
This will mark award-winning singer Aisha Retno first time involving with theatre production. — Picture by Raymond Manuel

To manage the demanding physical, vocal, and cultural demands of the Javanese courtly roles, Tiara implemented a dual-casting strategy for Gusti Puteri, pairing Mila with pop powerhouse and songwriter Aisha Retno.
Contrary to public speculation regarding rivalry, both performers view the arrangement as a collaborative sisterhood of craft.
“We are completely different performers and people.
“My mother showed one side of Gusti Putri twenty years ago – The Princess was a historical figure with a million facets.
“In a two-and-a-half-hour show, Aisha will reveal one side, and I will reveal another. There is zero competition between us,” Mila said.
For Aisha, a Universiti Malaya economics graduate making her musical theatre debut, the transition from commercial recording artist to stage actor required shedding her pop identity entirely.
“I know some people might buy tickets expecting to see ‘Aisha Retno,’ but my goal is to make sure there is no Aisha Retno on that stage,” Aisha explains.
“As a singer-songwriter, you spend years hiding your pain—even if you’re unwell, you put on a happy face for the audience.
“But acting allows you to be vulnerable, raw, and broken, you get to channel real life experiences—like a heartbreak—directly into the dialogue.”

Aisha, whose mother possesses Javanese roots and personal experience in keraton (royal palace) traditions, credits both her family and Assistant Director Sabrina Hassan for helping her navigate the intense psychological demands of stepping into character without bringing the heavy emotional weight home.

Not just that, Tiara was also fascinated by Aisha’s grounded professionalism, pointing out that despite a punishing schedule of traveling and out-of-state shows, she arrives punctually for rehearsals without pretense— which Tiara describes as a rare degree of dedication for an established artist.

Aside from the dual-casting role strategy for Gusti Puteri, Tiara also uses the same approach with Bayan, Gusti Puteri’s loyal lady-in-waiting, which is split between singer Mimifly and actress-singer Nadia Aqilah.
The tormented Laksamana
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Potraying the legendary Hang Tuah is a dream come true for actor and singer Aqasha. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
Opposite the Princess stands the legendary Hang Tuah, portrayed by actor and singer Aqasha.
For Aqasha, taking on the legendary warrior is the realisation of a two-decade journey that began when he served as an understudy in the show’s original 2006 run.
“I’ve spent twenty years dreaming of this and I am a fan of this show, its poetic literature, and its score first and foremost.
“When I was an understudy twenty years ago, my younger self focused mostly on the romantic, ‘lovey-dovey’ aspect of falling in love with the Princess.
“But coming back to it today, I see Tuah through a completely different lens,” Aqasha said.
Rather than playing a romantic hero or an untouchable martial arts archetype, Aqasha grounds his portrayal in internal conflict.
“This time, I’m exploring how Tuah serves the Sultan and what his loyalty to Melaka truly costs him – Is he just another general living off wages, or is he a man bound by an unbreakable oath?
“He is a deeply tormented man– torn between his personal desire for love and his unyielding duty to his sovereign,” he said.

Rather than fearing comparisons, Aqasha encourages audiences to view the production through the lens of musical storytelling—focusing on themes of love, duty, and sacrifice—to fully appreciate the character’s emotional depth.
The legend returns
From the royal courts of Majapahit to the mighty Sultanate of Melaka and the mist-shrouded heights of Gunung Ledang, PGL tells an epic tale of love, loyalty, power and sacrifice.
After months of preparations, PGL will be premiering its first full show today with all 23,000 tickets already sold out since August for its 15-day run.

Although there’s no update of any new added dates for its JCPAC run, PGL will be making its way to Singapore next year.

As confirmed by theatre venue Esplanade Singapore via its social media, PGL is set to arrive at Singapore shores in part of its Pesta Raya - Malay Festival of Arts in April next year with priority bookings set to open starting from November 4 to November 10.
The Singapore run will also feature the same lineup of the new generation of cast.

Apart from the cast, PGL also boasts an experienced creative team with visual projections overseen by Datuk Yusry Abdul Halim of KRU Studios, wardrobe creations by Singaporean couturier Fatimah Mohsin, stagecraft by scenic designer Raja Malik, and backstage operations led by Tiara’s long-time technical director, Roslidah “Cik Lid” Ali.
2aa0e905b74323ee: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — The tax literacy programme implemented by the Inland Revenue Board of Malaysia (IRB) throughout the 2026 HASiL Month has involved nearly 300,000 taxpayers nationwide.
Its chief executive officer, Datuk Dr Abu Tariq Jamaluddin, said various programmes were implemented throughout October to raise public awareness of taxation and the agency’s role.

“During this period, we have conducted several activities, including the HASiL Literacy Tour, under which we have carried out 251 tours across the country to engage with communities and explain issues related to taxation,” he told reporters during the closing ceremony of the 2026 HASiL Month here today.
Abu Tariq noted that IRB also received nearly 50,000 responses through surveys to gather public opinions on taxation and the services provided by the agency.
He said the feedback included views collected this year as well as in previous years.

“Among the focuses of the 2026 HASiL Month is promoting the voluntary declaration programmes for stamp duty and e-Invoice, with the stamp duty programme ending at the end of this year and the e-Invoice programme at the end of next year,” he said.
Meanwhile, he said IRB also encourages the public to provide information about individuals or companies suspected of underreporting their taxes through the e-Tax Escape platform.
“The information we receive will be kept confidential,” he added. — Bernama

* Editor’s note: HASiL is the Inland Revenue Board of Malaysia’s brand name. It comes from the Malay word “hasil”, meaning revenue, and is not a strict acronym. The board’s Malay name is Lembaga Hasil Dalam Negeri.

461e783471b0f1d0: KUALA LUMPUR: Aaron Tai-Yap Roy King are no longer an experimental pair.

National men's doubles coach Herry Iman Pierngadi has confirmed the explosive new combination as a permanent partnership in the build-up to the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics qualification campaign, which begins next year.
Aaron-Roy King showed their pedigree by winning their first World Tour title together at the Super 500 Arctic Open three weeks ago before reaching the Hylo Open semi-finals on Friday.
The world No. 74 Malaysians after just three tournaments together, crushed Taiwan's fifthseeds Chiu Hsiang Chieh-Wang Chi Lin 21-16, 21-17 in just 30 minutes.
It was their second consecutive victory over a top-15 combination, having stunned Indonesia's world No. 7 and top seeds Sabar Karyaman-Moh Reza Isfahani 22-20, 21-19 in Thursday's second round.
Their latest triumph was impressive as they overcame a pair featuring two-time Olympic gold medallist - Chi Lin, who won both titles alongside former partner Lee Yang.
Aaron-Roy King's performance was also notable given Herry's absence, where the young duo were guided by men's doubles assistant coach Muhammad Miftakh.

However, Herry was not surprised by their overall performance in Europe and added that the pair were well suited to the 15-point scoring format, which will be officially introduced at all tournaments by the Badminton World Federation (BWF) in January.
"Yes, Aaron Tai-Roy King have been confirmed as a permanent pair as they have shown their true quality," said Herry.
"In fact, they were combined specifically with the 15-point scoring format in mind, as it will be used at the 2028 Olympics."
Their emergence will see a more intense Olympic qualification race, which runs from May 3 next year to April 28, 2028.
World No. 4 Aaron Chia-Soh Wooi Yik and independent world No. 5 Goh Sze Fei-Nur Izzuddin Rumsani will also be involved in the battle for the two available men's doubles spots in Los Angeles.
"It's a good situation. Everyone has the ability and the chance (to qualify for LA28)," said Herry.
Aaron-Roy King will face Danish pair Christian Faust Kjaer-Rasmus Kjaer for a place in the final late today.
The Malaysians had beaten the Danes at the same stage en route to their Arctic Open triumph.
"I believe they can go all the way," added Herry.
Meanwhile, independent mixed doubles pair Hoo Pang Ron-Lai Pei Jing secured their third consecutive semi-final appearance at the Hylo Open on Friday.

Fresh from reaching the last four at the Denmark Open two weeks ago and finishing runners-up at the French Open last week, world No. 24 Pang Ron-Pei Jing advanced to the semi-finals in Saarbrucken, Germany, with a 21-17, 21-17 victory over Hong Kong's Chan Yin Chak-Ng Tsz Yau in 31 minutes.
They will take on French world champions Thom Gicquel-Delphine Delrue later today.

It has been a spectacular run for the duo following 28-year-old Pang Ron's departure from the BA of Malaysia (BAM) by mutual consent in May, while 34-year-old Pei Jing was contemplating her future after her partner Jimmy Wong joined the national squad around the same time.
It was practically a swap, with Jimmy teaming up with Pang Ron's former partner, Cheng Su Yin.

554d641925cf6669: MELAKA, Oct 31 — Enhancing digital education facilities is among the key priorities of Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate for the Bukit Katil state seat, Adly Zahari, should he be given the mandate in the 16th Melaka state election.

The incumbent said the effort was important to ensure that the younger generation in the constituency benefited from developments in digital technology, particularly in education, security and economic development.

The Amanah vice-president is facing a four-cornered contest against Perikatan Nasional (PN) candidate Ridzuan Sarif, Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) candidate Dr Aliza Che Amran and independent candidate Abu Bakar Sabudin.

Adly, who is also Deputy Defence Minister, said digital education should be given priority, as a digitally literate generation could benefit the education sector while also contributing to stronger economic capabilities now and in the future.
He also said that completing the construction of a polyclinic in the constituency was another matter that needed attention.
“We have already obtained approval from the Ministry of Health (MOH), and we have secured the budget,” he said.

However, he said his eight years of service in the Bukit Katil state constituency, including during the 22 months when PH was in government, provided a basis for voters to assess his track record.
“So, we (PH) leave it to the people to assess all the efforts we have made, and we will continue to serve them regardless of the outcome. We will certainly respect whatever decision the people make.

In the 15th Melaka state election, Adly secured a majority of 1,057 votes after defeating three other candidates, namely Datuk Hasnoor Sdg Husin of BN, Muhammad Al Afiz Yahya of PN and independent candidate Abdul Hamid.

a892ae1ac391f6a7: KUALA LUMPUR: Chickens found to have died before slaughter do not meet halal requirements, the Malaysian Islamic Development Department (Jakim) said, following a raid on an abattoir in Puchong, Selangor.
Jakim director-general Datuk Dr Sirajuddin Suhaimee said if the claims were confirmed, the chickens would not meet the requirements for halal slaughter.
"Under Islamic law, animals that are permissible for consumption must be slaughtered in accordance with the conditions stipulated by syarak.

"One of these conditions is that the chickens must still be alive when slaughtered. In other words, if the chickens had died before slaughter, they would be considered carrion," he said when contacted today.

It was reported that more than 6.5 tonnes of raw chicken suspected of being processed without complying with Islamic slaughter requirements and halal certification standards had been seized in a raid on a warehouse in Puchong two days ago.
Sirajuddin said the department viewed the matter seriously as it involved compliance with Islamic law, hygiene and public confidence in the halal status of chicken supplies in the market.
"Based on initial inspections, the premises were suspected of carrying out the slaughter, processing and distribution of fresh chicken without permits or approval from the local authorities.

"Companies operating without valid permits or licences are not eligible to apply for the Malaysian Halal Certification (SPHM), as one of the requirements for certification is to obtain a municipal council licence," he said.
On the distribution of chicken supplies from the abattoir, he said the premises were not holders of SPHM issued by Jakim.

"Therefore, any sales records from the premises are not included in Jakim's halal certification monitoring records. In this matter, the relevant authorities must act within their respective jurisdictions.
"Action to trace and recall chicken already in the market must take into account the provisions of existing laws.
"Relevant enforcement agencies can take action within their respective jurisdictions to stop sales, segregate stocks and carry out recalls or seize identified supplies," he said.
7e00e0df0ac9ef05: DAKAR, Oct 31 — The 2026 Youth Olympic Games, the first Olympics ever to be held on African soil, open today in the Senegalese capital marking an historic moment for the continent.
Signs proclaiming “Africa welcomes, Dakar celebrates” are abundant across Dakar, which is hosting some 2,665 young competitors aged 14 to 17 from around the world.
The event marks the return of Russian athletes to the Olympics and also includes a refugee team. Overall, the athletes will compete across 25 sports and 153 medal events.

“We’ve got people from around the world that maybe had a very different idea about Africa and they’re going to leave, hopefully, with something really positive in mind”, International Olympic Committee (IOC) President Kirsty Coventry, a former Zimbabwean swimmer, said Thursday during a press conference in Dakar.
“I think that is really important for our continent”, she said.
Events ranging from athletics to beach wrestling, rugby sevens to breaking, will be held across eight venues in three locations.
Dakar, the nearby suburb of Diamniadio and the beach town of Saly located some 80 kilometres (50 miles) from the capital, will all host events.
Sports culture
An opening ceremony today evening in Diamniadio will kick off the Games.
A total of 136 Senegalese athletes will participate in the Youth Olympics, with some 6,000 volunteers from Senegal helping put on the event.
The west African nation is renowned for its sports culture, including its football team, traditional wrestling and surf scene.
Football enthusiasts and young people often organise impromptu matches in the evenings or weekends on the beach or in village squares.
And as the day cools, hundreds of people flock to Dakar’s iconic coastal road, the Corniche, to run, do strength training or take part in group exercise.
While a sense of excitement is beginning to stir in the capital, the fourth summer edition of the Youth Olympics have struggled to stoke wild enthusiasm across Senegal.
Many are more concerned with the high cost of living, unemployment and economic hardship.
“Once the youth Olympic Games in Senegal begin, Dakar will become the capital of African youth,” Senegal Prime Minister Ahmadou Al Aminou Lo said in an interview with AFP this week.
“Africa hosting the (Youth) Olympic Games, it’s a symbol”, he said.
Russian athletes

With the IOC effectively lifting the Russian Olympic Committee’s (ROC) suspension in July, the Youth Games will mark the first Olympic competition since Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in early 2022 in which Russian athletes are allowed to compete under their own flag and colours.
According to the ROC, 13 Russian athletes will participate and 10 coaches will accompany them to Senegal.

“The kids are excited, it’s good news that our legitimate right to participate with the national anthem and Russian flag has been restored”, Anzor Gaunov, who coaches Anastasia Dobrovolskaya in judo, told AFP earlier this month in Moscow.
However, it is up to each sport’s international federation whether to authorise the Russian athletes’ participation.
The Dakar Youth Games will also welcome a refugee Olympic team, composed primarily of athletes based in Africa.
The IOC has called the Dakar Games an important milestone for the continent and an opportunity to showcase Senegal’s cultural richness and Africa’s growing role within the Olympics.

South Africa could potentially become the first African nation to host the Olympic Games, having already paved the way by hosting the men’s FIFA World Cup in 2010. The country is officially in the running for the 2036 Summer Olympics. — AFP
fb1a7d871c729b89: JOHOR BARU: Police are exploring ways to expand their collaboration with Media Prima Bhd (MPB), including participating in future 'Karnival Jom Heboh' events to provide more services directly to the public.

She said the association hoped to continue its collaboration with the carnival at its next venue, Stadium Merdeka in Kuala Lumpur.

2756a093010d4be2: MELAKA, Oct 31 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) has set its stance of not compromising and rejecting the politics of hatred, incitement and narrow racial narratives throughout the 16th Melaka state election campaign.

PH secretary-general Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the coalition chose to highlight the campaign based on the theme ‘Melaka Rumah Kita’, focusing on competing ideas, service records and the welfare of the people.

Saifuddin Nasution, who is also the Home Minister, explained that victory in the election is not judged by which party is the most vocal in inciting hostility, but rather by which party is most trusted to be able to defend the fate of the community.

“Our red line is to completely reject the politics of hatred, the politics of incitement and politics that is based on the idea that to defend our race, we must oppress other races. For our race to succeed, other races have no place... we completely reject that.

“We will focus on a peaceful campaign, because we are convinced that an election campaign is not measured by the victory of which party is the loudest, but who is actually the most trusted and credible,” he said at a press conference at the PH Main Operations Room here today.

Commenting further, Saifuddin Nasution said the three main messages that PH brought in the election campaign this time were to celebrate the festival of democracy by respecting differences of opinion; to highlight policy offers and the ability to solve problems; and to launch a manifesto that focuses on job opportunities, the cost of living and the future of the youth.

Touching on the direction of the campaign, Saifuddin Nasution explained that PH would not entertain any political speculation regarding the new alignment after the election, but instead would focus fully on reaching out to voters including out-of-constituency voters.

“The out-of-constituency voter segment is indeed included in the electoral machinery’s checklist. We have accurate figures for each seat contested regarding out-of-constituency voters, and they are the focus of our attention to be contacted to ensure they return to vote,” he explained.
The EC has set November 14 as the polling day for the Melaka election while early voting is on November 10.
For the latest news on the 16th Melaka polls, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/. — Bernama
1795db283bcbe184: MELAKA: Pakatan Harapan has pledged to conduct a peaceful campaign throughout the Melaka election, having learnt that electoral victory should not be determined by who shouts the loudest, but by who earns the people's trust.

Its secretary-general Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said PH had drawn a firm line against the politics of hatred and division, with the aim of ensuring peaceful political competition without undermining racial harmony.

He said the coalition had outlined three key messages for its campaign namely respecting differences of opinion in a democracy, ensuring the contest remained free from slander and personal attacks, and offering solutions through its election manifesto.

"Our red line is that we completely reject the politics of hatred and division, as well as the belief that defending our own race requires us to oppress others, or that for our race to succeed, other communities must have no place.
"We reject this outright. This is our campaign principle and our red line," he said at a press conference at the PH Melaka main operations centre here today.
Also present were Melaka PKR chairman Adam Adli and DAP representative Young Syefura Othman.

Saifuddin said the first message would be reflected in PH's commitment to peaceful campaigning, adding that electoral victory should not be determined by who shouted the loudest, but by who earned the people's trust.
He said the second message was aimed at ensuring the campaign did not become a platform for slander or personal attacks, allowing voters to assess the proposals put forward by each candidate.
"This is not a contest of slander, much less a competition over who can launch the strongest personal attacks.
"It is about choosing ideas, policies, track records, solutions to problems and the people's welfare," he said.
On the third message, Saifuddin said PH would elaborate on its proposals through its election manifesto, which would be launched soon.
He said the manifesto would include measures to create employment opportunities and address issues concerning the future of young people.
Meanwhile, Saifuddin said PH was fielding 24 candidates from its three component parties: 10 from PKR and seven each from DAP and Amanah.
He said the coalition was offering a combination of experienced candidates and new faces whom it believed could put forward meaningful proposals to voters in their respective constituencies.

Saifuddin said PH's campaign slogan, "Melaka Rumah Kita" (Melaka Our Home), reflected its vision of the state as a peaceful and harmonious place where people of different races, religions and cultures could live together.
09cdf029c47271e2: PEKAN: Universiti Malaysia Pahang Al-Sultan Abdullah (UMPSA) is strengthening its position as a globally competitive technical university through academic development, international dual-degree programmes and industry collaborations to produce competent graduates who meet labour market demands.

UMPSA Vice-Chancellor Professor Ts Dr Yatimah Alias said international recognition, academic excellence, impactful research and global networks were key to positioning the university as a regional hub for advanced Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET).

She said UMPSA continued to explore innovative teaching approaches to equip graduates with technical knowledge, professional skills and the ability to adapt to the changing demands of global industries.

"International collaborations, industry-based learning and strategic research are among UMPSA's strengths in providing a comprehensive learning experience while enhancing graduate employability," she said.
DUAL-DEGREE PROGRAMMES FOR GLOBAL COMPETITIVENESS

UMPSA currently offers 14 dual-degree programmes in collaboration with higher education institutions in China, Germany, South Korea and Kazakhstan, involving nearly 500 students, or about 4.5 per cent of its total undergraduate population.

Among the university's strategic partners are Karlsruhe University of Applied Sciences (HKA) and Technische Hochschule Mannheim (THM) in Germany; Beijing Jiaotong University (BJTU) and Tianjin University in China; Kazakh National Agrarian Research University (KazNARU) in Kazakhstan; and Hanyang University ERICA Campus in South Korea.

The collaboration with HKA, which is now in its 16th year, is among the benchmarks of UMPSA's international engineering education, offering dual-degree programmes that combine academic learning with industrial exposure.

UMPSA has also expanded its international partnerships through a postgraduate dual-degree programme in civil engineering with Chongqing University in China, as well as master's and Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) programmes in aerospace with Central Queensland University (CQU), Australia.
The dual-degree programmes in Kazakhstan are expected to broaden UMPSA's collaboration in agricultural technology and food security.

UMPSA has strengthened its internationalisation drive through a dual-degree partnership with China's Ningxia University, offering a Bachelor of Manufacturing Engineering Technology (Advanced Manufacturing) programme.

This year marks the graduation of the programme's first cohort, highlighting the partnership's role in producing globally competitive graduates with international exposure and strong technological competencies.
To date, 106 Ningxia University students are currently enrolled in the UMPSA-Ningxia University dual-degree programme.

The achievement underscores UMPSA's commitment to strengthening international academic ties, broadening cross-border learning opportunities and producing globally competitive engineering and technology graduates.

As part of efforts to strengthen its academic ecosystem, UMPSA has upgraded several entities, including the Advanced TVET Academy, Institute of Advanced Integrated Studies (IAIS) and Faculty of Applied Language Studies.

The upgrading of the Centre for Modern Languages to the Faculty of Applied Language Studies has expanded the university's role in producing graduates with strong communication skills, language proficiency and cross-cultural competencies to meet the demands of the global workforce.

UMPSA has also introduced new academic programmes, including the East Coast's first Master of Halal Industry Management by coursework, Bachelor of Technology in Facilities Management with Honours, Master of Competency Based Talent Management and Master of Integrated Engineering Management.
Meanwhile, UMPSA's Global Classroom initiative recorded a 41.3 per cent increase in participation between 2025 and 2026, from 4,388 to 6,202 participants.

The growth reflects the expansion of international learning opportunities through partnerships with universities in Japan, Singapore, China and the United States, further promoting cross-cultural interaction among students.

With a graduate employability rate of 97.2 per cent in 2025, UMPSA continues to emphasise practical learning, professional competency development and industry partnerships to ensure its graduates meet labour market requirements.
The university also received the TVET Industry Collaboration & Research Award at the Malaysia Education & TVET Awards 2026, recognising its commitment to strengthening industry ties and research.
RESEARCH AND INNOVATION DRIVE DEVELOPMENT

UMPSA is strengthening its research, innovation and technology transfer ecosystem through the establishment of several new Centres of Excellence (CoEs) focusing on strategic fields and industry needs.
These include aerospace technology, climate-resilient infrastructure, rare earth elements and critical minerals, all of which are of strategic importance to the country's technological development.

UMPSA is also studying the establishment of the Tun Abdul Razak Centre for Legacy and Strategic Foresight to link its academic and research expertise with the legacy of the late prime minister, particularly in education, rural development, the economy, industrialisation and human capital development.

Through its Advanced TVET Academy, UMPSA is spearheading the Asia-Pacific Advanced TVET Hub (APATH), a regional platform involving 20 institutions and organisations from nine countries to promote technology-, innovation- and industry-driven TVET development.

The network provides opportunities for collaboration in micro-credential offerings, joint programmes, Global Classroom initiatives, international mobility, cross-border industrial training and industry-led joint research.
INCLUSIVE ECOSYSTEM AND SUSTAINABILITY

UMPSA is also advancing its inclusivity agenda through the Centre for Inclusive Technology and Ecosystem (iNKLUSIF), ensuring that technological advancements benefit all communities, including vulnerable groups and persons with disabilities (OKU).

Its initiatives include the Inclusive Technology and Ecosystem Hub (HATi) and collaboration with the DAMAi Community-Based Rehabilitation Organisation (PPDK) to widen access to technology and promote inclusive learning environments.
To empower students, initiatives such as Job on Campus, Student Apprenticeship and the management of 'Siswa Mall' aim to enhance their skills and develop their talents.
In terms of sustainability, UMPSA was named Malaysia's most sustainable university in the under-50-year-old category and ranked third among local universities in the UI GreenMetric 2026 rankings.

Ahead of its Silver Jubilee celebrations in 2027, UMPSA's research excellence was further recognised, with 27 researchers earning places on the World's Top 2% Scientists 2026 list, based on data released by Elsevier BV and Stanford University.

"This recognition encourages UMPSA to continuously enhance the quality of education, drive impactful innovations and nurture graduates who can contribute to the development of Pahang, Malaysia and the global community," she said.
UMPSA will continue to integrate technical education, internationalisation, research, industry collaboration and inclusivity to produce quality graduates and strengthen its global competitiveness.
Meanwhile, Dewan Tuanku Canselor, which features a design inspired by Pahang's traditional 'wau pungguk' kite, will host the university's 21st Convocation Ceremony for the first time.
The hall was inaugurated by UMPSA Chancellor, the Sultan of Pahang Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri'ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah.
A total of 3,345 graduates are scheduled to receive their scrolls during the ceremony, which will be held from Oct 31 to Nov 3.

354c34740a29c215: KUANTAN, Oct 31 — The National Autism Society of Malaysia plans to develop an autism village to provide safe accommodation for adult autistic individuals who have nowhere to live in Pahang.

The intention was expressed following the presence of the Tengku Ampuan of Pahang Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah to officiate the society’s Kuantan 2026 Charity Sale Ceremony at Taman Gelora here, today.

The society’s patron Datuk Megat Ahmad Shahrani Megat Sharuddin said the proposed development of the village aimed to ensure that autistic individuals aged 30 to 50, especially those who no longer have guardians, received suitable accommodation and continuous care.
He said the centre was proposed to accommodate about 200 residents with an estimated development cost of about RM25 million based on a study conducted.

“When their parents are gone, some of them do not have siblings or family members to take the responsibility of caring for them. We want to provide a place so that they are not abandoned,” he told reporters after the event.
Megat Ahmad Shahrani said his party was trying to obtain five acres of land and hoped that the proposal would receive the attention and support of the Pahang Royal Institution to realise the wish.
He said Pahang also had the potential to become a settlement for autistic individuals from all over the country and not just those from the state.

“The society is also trying to obtain financial support from corporate companies and related bodies to finance the project, but providing land is the main requirement before fundraising efforts can be intensified,” he said.

Meanwhile, he said the operating costs of the society’s centres nationwide reached about RM7 million a year, while the collection obtained was only around RM4 million, causing the association to have to find an additional RM3 million every year.

He said the cost of providing education and therapy for individuals with autism was high because the learning approach required more specific attention, with a low teacher-to-student ratio to ensure that the needs of each individual could be met.

“The society, however, strives to ensure that the fees charged remain affordable for all levels of society, in addition to providing assistance to underprivileged families based on an assessment of their circumstances,” he said. — Bernama

0702acbe158b4ee9: MASJID TANAH: Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today reiterated his proposal that Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh remain as Melaka Chief Minister if Barisan Nasional wins the state election.

523b484e11cebc90: PETALING JAYA: Three organisations representing the Chinese community in Melaka have submitted a memorandum to four political parties taking part in the Nov 14 state election, urging them to focus on policies when campaigning while respecting one another.

The memorandum was handed over by the Melaka Chinese Assembly Hall, Melaka Chinese School Boards Association and Malacca Chinese Chamber of Commerce and Industry during a two-hour meeting with representatives from DAP, PKR, MCA and Bersama yesterday.

Party leaders who attended the meeting included Melaka DAP chief Khoo Poay Tiong, acting state PKR chief Adam Adli, Melaka MCA operations room director Yong Fun Juan, and Bersama leader Lee Chean Chung.
Melaka Chinese Assembly Hall chairman Piong Yew Peng said the three groups wanted to transcend partisan politics while remaining engaged in the state's political affairs, Oriental Daily reported.

"On behalf of the Chinese community, we take this opportunity to appeal to all parties contesting the election to focus their campaigns on explaining their governance plans and policy directions, rather than resorting to unconstructive personal attacks against their opponents.

"Both ruling and opposition parties should respect one another and raise the standard of political competition through healthy policy debates, providing voters with a mature and clean political environment," he said.
Piong said the organisations had organised a roundtable with 30 associations across the state on Oct 1, with nearly 100 people attending.
He added that the memorandum submitted to the political parties was a compilation of the views of these grassroots community leaders.
"It is not merely a list of unilateral demands, but a constructive assessment by the Chinese community of Melaka's development."
He said the document had four sections with 46 policy proposals, covering governance, economy, education, culture, transport, healthcare and social welfare.
Piong expressed hope that the political parties would heed the views of the community leaders and consider adopting the proposals in their manifestos and policy agenda.
30a8afe03686952f: IPOH, Oct 31 — Police are tracking down suspects involved in a shooting incident in which several shots were fired at a BMW in front of a house in Taman Hijau, Kampung Koh, near Sitiawan, yesterday.
Manjung police chief ACP Hasbullah Abd Rahman said that police received a report from a man at 1.54 pm yesterday regarding the incident.

He said investigations revealed that the incident was believed to have occurred at 4.16 am on the same day, when the complainant, who was inside his house, heard what sounded like gunshots. The complainant later discovered about 9 am that there were four bullet marks on the right-side door of his vehicle.
“A review of closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage at the scene showed two unidentified suspects approaching the vehicle on a motorcycle,” he said in a statement today.

“One of the suspects then fired shots at the vehicle before fleeing. Police have opened an investigation paper and the case is being investigated under Section 39 of the Arms Act 1960,” he said, adding that efforts to track down the suspects were ongoing.

Hasbullah said members of the public with any information on the incident were urged to come forward at the Manjung district police headquarters (IPD) or contact its Operations Room at 05-688 6222, the WhatsApp hotline at 017-682 8005, or any nearby police station.

Meanwhile, in a separate statement, Hasbullah said police had arrested a man and two women, aged between 24 and 26, on suspicion of being involved in the theft of a Toyota Hilux belonging to a man in Taman Mas 2, Sitiawan.
He said the three suspects had been remanded for six days, from October 28 to November 2, to facilitate investigations under Section 379A of the Penal Code.

“At about 5.30 pm on October 27, a team of police personnel from the Manjung IPD arrested all three suspects, who were believed to be involved in the incident. Police also seized a car key reader device believed to have been used in the vehicle thefts, as well as several other items.

“Interrogations found that the suspects admitted to being involved in eight vehicle theft cases, four in Perak and four in Kuala Lumpur, using the same modus operandi and targeting four-wheel-drive vehicles,” he said. — Bernama

* Editor’s note: The initials IPD stands for Ibu Pejabat Polis Daerah in Malay. Section 379A of the Penal Code concerns the theft of a motor vehicle or any of its component parts, and carries imprisonment of between one and seven years upon conviction, and the offender is also liable to a fine.

e50a104e4d71c40b: WASHINGTON: A record 47.9 million Americans have already voted in next week's US midterm elections, with participation surging in key battleground states and registered Democrats outpacing Republicans, figures showed on Friday.
The University of Florida's Election Lab had recorded 47,922,669 early votes nationwide by midday, surpassing the previous midterm record of 45.9 million cast ahead of Election Day in 2022.
The surge is especially pronounced in states with fiercely contested Senate races that could determine control of the chamber during the final two years of President Donald Trump's presidency.
In Texas, more than six million people had voted early by Wednesday, according to official figures, with in-person turnout running about 50 per cent ahead of the same stage in 2022.

North Carolina's election board reported early voting was up nearly 37 per cent compared with the same point four years ago, while South Carolina surpassed its entire 2022 early vote total on Monday, with five days of early voting still to go.

In Kansas, where Republican Senator Roger Marshall faces a tough re-election fight, advance ballots were running about two-thirds ahead of 2022 last week, according to the secretary of state's office.
In states that record voters' party affiliation, registered Democrats have accounted for a substantially larger share of early ballots than Republicans.
Election Lab figures showed Democrats making up about 44 per cent of early voters in those states, compared with 31 per cent for Republicans and 25 per cent for unaffiliated or minor-party voters.

University of Florida political scientist Michael McDonald, who oversees the Election Lab, has pointed to rising participation among Black and Hispanic voters in states that report racial and ethnic data, with particularly strong turnout in heavily Hispanic communities along the Texas-Mexico border.
In Georgia, where early in-person voting broke the state's midterm record on Thursday, women accounted for 56 per cent of ballots cast by that day, compared with 44 per cent for men.
"Georgians continue to head to the polls in record numbers because they trust the system," top elections official Brad Raffensperger said on Thursday.
But experts warn against interpreting the figures as a prediction of the election outcome.
A voter's party registration does not reveal which candidates they supported, and tens of millions more Americans are expected to cast ballots on Tuesday.
In recent elections, Republicans have tended to turn out in greater numbers on Election Day, potentially narrowing or reversing the Democrats' early advantage.
And higher early participation does not necessarily translate into higher overall turnout, since some voters may simply be casting their ballots sooner than in previous elections.
959857f219f1141c: AYER KEROH: Calon Pakatan Harapan (PH) bagi DUN Tanjung Bidara Yunazri Mustamiri akui berdepan laluan sukar untuk menewaskan penyandang Ab Rauf Yusoh namun menganggap ia tidak mustahil untuknya mencipta kejutan pada PRN Melaka kali ini.

6b7977eff67af2e2: MIRI, Oct 31 — Four men have been arrested by Miri police in connection with paint-splashing vandalism cases linked to illegal online moneylending activities in the division.

Miri District Police Chief ACP Mohd Farhan Lee Abdullah said in a statement late Friday that the suspects were detained in four separate operations conducted in Kampung Pujut Tanjong Batu on October 23 and 26.

He said the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) of Miri District Police Headquarters (IPD Miri) initially received a police report at 3.11pm on October 22 from a 54-year-old local man regarding an incident in which red paint was splashed on the front gate and porch floor of his house in Miri.
According to the complainant, the act was believed to be connected to demands for repayment of an online loan allegedly taken by his son.
The complainant discovered the incident around 10pm on October 21, after reviewing closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage at his residence in Jalan Acorus 7 here.
“The footage showed two unidentified men arriving at the house before one of them splashed red paint on the front gate and the floor at the front of the house.

“Prior to the incident, the complainant had received messages from an individual using the name ‘Kelvin’, demanding repayment of an online loan allegedly taken by his son. The messages also contained threats should the payment not be made,” said Mohd Farhan.

Based on the complainant’s information, his son had previously borrowed money online from an individual believed to be involved in unlicensed moneylending activities. Although the earlier debt was said to have been settled, his son later informed him that he had taken another RM200 loan from a different online lender.
“Acting on intelligence and the findings of investigations, a team of CID officers from IPD Miri arrested four local men aged between 25 and 32.
“Police investigations found that all four suspects were involved in the reported paint-splashing vandalism cases, enabling police to solve two cases reported on October 20 and October 22,” he said.

Following the arrests, police seized several items from the suspects, including mobile phones, clothing, slippers, two helmets allegedly worn during the incidents and two motorcycles believed to have been used in the incidents.
Both cases are being investigated under Section 427 of the Penal Code, which carries a penalty of one to five years’ imprisonment, a fine, or both, upon conviction.
Mohd Farhan said police take seriously any acts of intimidation, criminal mischief and threats that could jeopardise public safety and order.

He advised the public not to entertain threats or suspicious demands related to online loans and to lodge a police report immediately if they became victims or had information regarding such activities. — The Borneo Post
* Editor’s note: The initials IPD stands for Ibu Pejabat Polis Daerah in Malay.
b18c67d8abb05597: DAKAR: The 2026 Youth Olympic Games, the first Olympics ever to be held on African soil, open Saturday in the Senegalese capital marking an historic moment for the continent.
Signs proclaiming "Africa welcomes, Dakar celebrates" are abundant across Dakar, which is hosting some 2,665 young competitors aged 14 to 17 from around the world.
The event marks the return of Russian athletes to the Olympics and also includes a refugee team. Overall, the athletes will compete across 25 sports and 153 medal events.

"We've got people from around the world that maybe had a very different idea about Africa and they're going to leave, hopefully, with something really positive in mind", International Olympic Committee (IOC) president Kirsty Coventry, a former Zimbabwean swimmer, said Thursday during a press conference in Dakar.
"I think that is really important for our continent", she said.
Events ranging from athletics to beach wrestling, rugby sevens to breaking, will be held across eight venues in three locations.
Dakar, the nearby suburb of Diamniadio and the beach town of Saly located some 80km from the capital, will all host events.
Sports culture
An opening ceremony Saturday evening in Diamniadio will kick off the Games.
A total of 136 Senegalese athletes will participate in the Youth Olympics, with some 6,000 volunteers from Senegal helping put on the event.
The west African nation is renowned for its sports culture, including its football team, traditional wrestling and surf scene.
Football enthusiasts and young people often organise impromptu matches in the evenings or weekends on the beach or in village squares.
And as the day cools, hundreds of people flock to Dakar's iconic coastal road, the Corniche, to run, do strength training or take part in group exercise.
While a sense of excitement is beginning to stir in the capital, the fourth summer edition of the Youth Olympics have struggled to stoke wild enthusiasm across Senegal.
Many are more concerned with the high cost of living, unemployment and economic hardship.
"Once the youth Olympic Games in Senegal begin, Dakar will become the capital of African youth," Senegal's prime minister Ahmadou Al Aminou Lo said in an interview with AFP this week.
"Africa hosting the (Youth) Olympic Games, it's a symbol", he said.
Russian athletes

With the IOC effectively lifting the Russian Olympic Committee's (ROC) suspension in July, the Youth Games will mark the first Olympic competition since Russia's invasion of Ukraine in early 2022 in which Russian athletes are allowed to compete under their own flag and colours.
According to the ROC, 13 Russian athletes will participate and 10 coaches will accompany them to Senegal.

"The kids are excited, it's good news that our legitimate right to participate with the national anthem and Russian flag has been restored", Anzor Gaunov, who coaches Anastasia Dobrovolskaya in judo, told AFP earlier this month in Moscow.
However, it is up to each sport's international federation whether to authorise the Russian athletes' participation.
The Dakar Youth Games will also welcome a refugee Olympic team, composed primarily of athletes based in Africa.
The IOC has called the Dakar Games an important milestone for the continent and an opportunity to showcase Senegal's cultural richness and Africa's growing role within the Olympics.

South Africa could potentially become the first African nation to host the Olympic Games, having already paved the way by hosting the men's Fifa World Cup in 2010. The country is officially in the running for the 2036 Summer Olympics.

1c2af7307feac39a: SEPANG: Jorge Martin has pulled out of the Petronas Grand Prix of Malaysia after conceding it was "too early" to race with a fractured wrist suffered in Australia last week.
Aprilia Racing withdrew the Spaniard ahead of qualifying this morning, following uncompetitive lap times across Friday's sessions and Saturday's second free practice (FP2).
Martin said his wrist could not withstand the demands of a full race distance, though he remained satisfied with his physical progress at the Sepang International Circuit.
"The healing process is going really fast, but not fast enough to be efficient on the bike," Martin said during a media scrum.
"I felt that I could ride for maybe one lap without pain, but then after that, I would have a lot of pain. So I could not be constant.

"After discussing with the team, we thought that I was doing too much to continue, yet with nothing to gain. It would be useless to keep riding for 20 laps and deteriorate the condition (of his wrist).
"It is better to wait and allow the bone to heal a little more. For sure, in Qatar I will feel better, but it was too early to race here."
Martin entered the Malaysian round in second place in the championship standings, 10 points behind leader Marc Marquez of Ducati Lenovo.
Martin said his title prospects appear dim given the injury, but insisted he will continue to fight.
"For sure, I will fight until the end, not just for me but also for my team and my people. I will try again in Qatar," he said.
"I tried here, and I couldn't do it, but this part of life, this is part of the sport.
"I was able to ride a MotoGP bike with a broken wrist and was under two minutes (a lap), so I am already proud of my performances here."
Martin added that he will continue therapy to accelerate his recovery.
Despite regional conflict in the Middle East, the Qatar GP remains scheduled for Nov 6-8.
Portimao (Nov 20-22) and Valencia (Nov 27-29) will stage the season's final two rounds.
f25a723e6fd09448: KUALA LUMPUR: Industri maritim Malaysia memerlukan sokongan pembiayaan lebih kukuh daripada bank tempatan bagi merealisasikan potensi pelaburan dan membolehkan pemain industri domestik mengembangkan operasi, khususnya dalam sektor pembekalan bahan api kapal (bunkering), kata Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif Maritime Network Sdn Bhd R Jeyenderan.
Perkhidmatan bunkering merangkumi pembekalan, penyimpanan dan pengurusan logistik bahan api marin, pelincir serta bekalan keperluan bagi kegunaan kapal dan vesel marin.

Jeyenderan berkata ramai pemain industri berminat untuk menceburi sektor itu, namun berdepan kesukaran mendapatkan pembiayaan bank kerana institusi kewangan tempatan menganggap perniagaan berkenaan berisiko tinggi, khususnya bagi pembiayaan pembelian kapal dan aset berkaitan aktiviti bunkering.

Beliau berkata pelabur dari Singapura lazimnya menyalurkan dana menerusi bank di negara itu dan bukannya institusi kewangan Malaysia, sekali gus menyebabkan potensi manfaat ekonomi mengalir ke luar negara.

"Mereka langsung tidak menggunakan khidmat bank kita. Ini memberikan kesan yang amat buruk dan kita tidak boleh menjalankan kegiatan amal di perairan sendiri. Perairan kita sangat indah dan mempunyai aliran trafik kapal yang baik.

"Akibatnya, kita kehilangan banyak sumbangan kepada keluaran dalam negara kasar (KDNK) kerana suatu ketika dahulu, jumlah pembekalan kita mencecah kira-kira 600,000 tan sehingga 2013, tetapi kini menurun kepada 200,000 tan," katanya dalam temu bual selepas menjadi tetamu program Ruang Bicara terbitan Bernama TV bertajuk "Industri Maritim: Cabaran Global, Impak Domestik" pada Jumaat.
Mengenai dasar, beliau berkata garis panduan lebih jelas diperlukan, khususnya berkaitan dokumentasi kastam yang meliputi urusan import, eksport dan proses lain berkaitan perkapalan.

Jeyenderan berkata pemain industri sering berdepan kesukaran memahami prosedur serta keperluan dokumentasi berbeza yang ditetapkan pelbagai agensi, termasuk Jabatan Kastam Diraja Malaysia (JKDM), Agensi Penguatkuasaan Maritim Malaysia (APMM), pihak berkuasa pelabuhan dan pengendali pelabuhan.

"Sebagai contoh, kita perlu mengetahui prosedur operasi standard (SOP) yang betul bagi mengemukakan dokumen K1 hingga K9. Prosedur ini perlu disahkan dan dimuat naik ke dalam sistem supaya semua pihak mematuhi keperluan yang sama," katanya.
Siri K1 hingga K9 merujuk kepada set borang pengisytiharan kastam standard yang ditadbir oleh JKDM di bawah Akta Kastam 1967.

Mengenai sasaran industri maritim Malaysia di bawah Rancangan Malaysia Ke-13 (RMK13) hingga 2030, Jeyenderan berkata industri itu secara keseluruhannya berada pada landasan yang betul, namun perlu meningkatkan pengurusan serta memastikan bahan buangan yang boleh digunakan sebagai bahan suapan bagi pengeluaran bahan api penerbangan mampan (SAF) dapat dikekalkan.
fb53352e9ef9b717: AFRIN: Seven people, including five children, have died and seven others were injured after torrential rains triggered flash floods in eastern Syria, authorities said on Friday.
Four people remain missing and rescue teams are continuing to search flooded areas, emergency and disaster management minister Raed al-Saleh said in a statement on X.
The five children drowned in pools of water formed by the floods, while another person died in a traffic accident, Saleh said, without providing details of the seventh death.
Flooding has hit the eastern provinces of Raqqa, Deir al-Zor and Hasakah, as well as parts of Aleppo, damaging infrastructure, cutting off roads and forcing families to leave their homes.

Syria's civil defence teams have carried out more than 550 emergency operations since the storms began, rescuing 60 people trapped by floodwater and responding to more than 900 distress calls, Saleh said.

Emergency crews evacuated more than 350 students from two schools and helped 375 families leave camps in Raqqa province. Teams also responded to flooding at camps in rural Aleppo and Idlib, and pumped water from around 250 homes and public buildings.

In Deir al-Zor, the floods damaged roads and telecommunications infrastructure, disrupting transport and communications, state news agency SANA reported. Heavy rainfall also caused seven culverts to collapse, cutting off access to several areas.
Authorities suspended classes in Raqqa, Hasakah and Deir al-Zor on Thursday, while forecasters warned unsettled weather could continue into Saturday.

99754ef3d81763e4: MELAKA: Umno and Pas must avoid disputes and set aside their differences to ensure their cooperation remains strong.

3493e00c68826a12: TUMPAT, Oct 31 — The public, particularly Muslims, have been urged to play a role in curbing the spread of deviant teachings that could undermine the sanctity of the faith by promptly reporting any suspicious activities to the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim) or the respective state Islamic religious authorities.

Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Zulkifli Hasan said the government had monitoring mechanisms in place through a committee tasked with coordinating the monitoring and control of teachings that could affect the sanctity of the faith.

He said the committee comprised Jakim, the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), the Ministry of Education (MOE), the Ministry of Higher Education (MOHE) and other relevant ministries.
“We are therefore closely monitoring any teachings that could undermine one’s faith,” he told Bernama after officiating the Organic Chicken Farming Project in Teluk Renjuna here today.

He was responding to questions on several videos that went viral on social media recently, allegedly showing Muslims taking part in non-Muslim religious rituals, prompting coordinated action between state Islamic religious authorities and the police.
Zulkifli said that, in certain cases, enforcement action was taken by state religious authorities in accordance with their respective jurisdictions and existing legal provisions.
He said Jakim also worked closely with state religious authorities to monitor the situation and ensure that the matter was addressed appropriately, while respecting ongoing legal proceedings.

In this regard, he encouraged the public to come forward with information or raise any questions concerning the matter with the state religious authorities or JAKIM to enable appropriate action to be taken. — Bernama
bb0a1157c9209ed9: KOTA KINABALU: The Pink Haven provides dignity, comfort and reassurance to breast cancer patients and their caregivers, said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor.
"For patients travelling from rural communities and other parts of Sabah to Kota Kinabalu for treatment, the journey can be physically exhausting, emotionally difficult and financially draining.
"Patients and caregivers may have to spend time away from their homes and families while coping with the uncertainty of a cancer diagnosis.
"It is a 'home away from home' that helps ease the burden of travelling for care," he said in a speech delivered at the launch of the centre established by Sabah Kinabalu Pink Ribbon (SKPR).
Assistant Minister of Women, Health and Community Wellbeing Datuk Rina Jainal delivered the speech on behalf of the chief minister.

Hajiji said the state government recognised the value of initiatives such as The Pink Haven and the importance of working with healthcare institutions, community organisations, donors and volunteers to support people affected by cancer.
He said he was pleased that the RM300,000 allocation he approved two years ago had helped bring the initiative into operation and was being put to good use.

He said that since its establishment in 2010, SKPR had raised awareness of breast cancer, supported patients and survivors, and helped families and communities better understand the importance of standing alongside those affected.
"With The Pink Haven, SKPR takes its work a step further by turning compassion into practical support," he said.

1b73b6559aa2c56c: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — Malaysia’s maritime industry is calling for a stronger financing support from local banks to unlock its investment potential and enable domestic players to expand their operations, particularly in the bunkering sector, said Maritime Network Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Datuk Seri Jeyenderan R.
Bunkering services refer to the supply, storage, and logistical management of marine fuels, lubricants, and essential provisions to power ships and marine vessels.

Jeyenderan said many industry players were interested in entering the sector but faced difficulties securing bank financing, as local banks considered the business high-risk, particularly when financing vessel and bunkering asset purchases.

He pointed out that investors from Singapore often channelled their funds through Singaporean banks instead of Malaysian financial institutions, resulting in potential economic benefits flowing out of the country.
“They don’t use our bankers at all. That has a very bad impact and we can’t be doing charity in our waters. We have very beautiful waters and we have good traffic going on.

“For that reason, we are losing a lot of gross domestic product. Back in the day, we were doing about 600,000 tonnes until 2013, but now, it’s down to 200,000 tonnes,” he said in an interview after appearing on Bernama TV’s Ruang Bicara programme titled “Maritime Industry: Global Challenges, Domestic Impact” yesterday.
On policies, he said clearer guidelines are needed particularly for customs documentation, covering import, export and other shipping-related processes.

Jeyenderan said industry players often face difficulties navigating different documentation procedures and requirements imposed by various agencies, including the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (RMCD), the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA), port authorities and port operators.

“For example, we need to know the proper standard operating procedure (SOP) for submitting documents from K1 to K9. These procedures must be confirmed and uploaded into the system so that everyone follows the same requirements,” he said.
The K1-K9 series refers to the standard family of customs declaration forms administered by the RMCD under the Customs Act 1967.

On Malaysia’s maritime industry targets under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP) up to 2030, Jeyenderan said it is generally on track to achieving them but needs to better manage and retain waste materials that could be used as feedstock for sustainable aviation fuel production. — Bernama
bfd8d7a38b8375e7: MUSCAT: Oman said Friday it had rescued 25 sailors from a merchant ship set ablaze in an attack, as Iran reported three oil tankers were halted while crossing the Strait of Hormuz.
Tehran has restricted maritime traffic through the strait since the Middle East war erupted on February 28 with US-Israeli strikes on the Islamic republic.
The narrow waterway, which normally carries about a fifth of global oil, has become a focal point of the conflict, with ships regularly coming under Iranian fire.

Muscat's navy "carried out an evacuation operation for 25 crew members of the merchant ship RITI, flying the Panamanian flag, after it was targeted, which led to a fire breaking out on board," Oman's Maritime Security Centre said in a statement.
The crew members were provided with medical care, the Omani statement said, without giving details.
The Marine Traffic ship-tracking website described the RITI as a crude oil tanker.
US Central Command chief Brad Cooper said in a video released on Friday that US forces had "successfully cleared the strait's internationally recognised primary transit routes of Iranian sea mines."
US forces remain "present to ensure that all primary transit routes in the Strait of Hormuz remain free and clear," he added.

Cooper said he visited some of the more than 50,000 US service members in the region, repeating earlier statements that Washington has helped Gulf countries export more than 1.5 billion barrels of crude via the strait since summer.
British maritime security agency UKMTO said that a ship 40 nautical miles (74 kilometres) south of Lavan island in Iran was struck on Friday by an unknown projectile, which caused a fire onboard.
"The crew of the vessel have been reported as safe and there is no reported environmental impact at this time," the UKMTO said on X.
BLOCKADE
Iran's Revolutionary Guards said earlier that three oil tankers had been halted after encountering unspecified "incidents" or hitting mines.

"Two offending oil tankers, one in the eastern part and the other in the western part of the Strait of Hormuz, which were attempting to pass through the unauthorised route, encountered incidents and were brought to a halt in the waters south of the strait," the IRGC said in a statement.

Iran has demanded that vessels use a designated route through the strait and coordinate their passage with the country's armed forces, labelling a southern corridor closer to Oman's shores as unauthorised.

The tankers had "switched off all their navigation and positioning systems and, with the support of the terrorist US military, were attempting to exit through the unauthorised route", the Guards' statement said.
The Guards did not specify the nature of the "incidents" the tankers encountered, which came a day after Iran's armed forces said at least four tankers had stopped in the area after hitting mines.
They said Friday's incidents occurred after the vessels received several radio warnings but disregarded them.

The IRGC said in a later statement that a supertanker carrying two million barrels of oil had stopped following an explosion "after striking a naval mine while navigating an unauthorised route through the Strait of Hormuz."
"This is the third oil tanker to have exploded and caught fire today as a result of attempting to pass through an unauthorised route," it added.
The United States has responded to Iran's blockade of the strait with a counterblockade of Iranian ports, further restricting Teheran's ability to export oil and conduct trade.

18a679116b516b4c: MELAKA, Oct 31 — A total of 79 candidates representing various political parties, coalitions and independents have been confirmed eligible to contest in the 16th Melaka State Election on Nov 14.

Election Commission (EC) chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said Pakatan Harapan (PH) would contest 24 seats, followed by Barisan Nasional (BN) with 23, Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) with 16 and Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) with seven.
Perikatan Nasional (PN) will contest five seats, Parti Pribumi Perkasa Malaysia (Putra) one seat, while three candidates will contest as independents.
“Of the 28 constituencies, there will be 11 straight fights, 11 three-cornered contests and six four-cornered contests.
“In terms of gender, there are 65 male candidates and 14 female candidates,” he told a press conference at the Ayer Keroh Federal Building here today.
Ramlan said the oldest candidate was Pakatan Harapan’s Telok Mas candidate Mohamad Jaafar, 66, while the youngest was the coalition’s Kuala Linggi candidate Muhammad Mukhlisul Mubin Julaisapiyah, 24.
He said two candidates were aged between 18 and 29, 14 between 30 and 39, 33 between 40 and 49, 22 between 50 and 59, and eight were aged 60 and above.
He added that the campaign period would run until 11.59 pm on Nov 13.
“The EC has established 28 Election Campaign Enforcement Teams (PP-KPR) to monitor the activities of all contesting candidates throughout the campaign period.
“The EC also hopes and reminds all parties to ensure that permitted campaign activities are conducted in a harmonious atmosphere and in compliance with the laws and regulations,” he said.
Ramlan also congratulated and commended all returning officers and their teams for ensuring the smooth conduct of today’s nomination proceedings.

“Appreciation and thanks are also extended to the Melaka State Secretary’s office and the departments and agencies under its purview, the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), the Attorney General’s Chambers, the Malaysian Department of Insolvency, the Ministry of Communications, media personnel, and all other parties involved, whether directly or indirectly,” he said.
The EC has set Nov 10 for early voting and Nov 14 as polling day for the 16th Melaka State Election.
For the latest news on the 16th Melaka State Election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/ — Bernama
71d76bcbd40d4e9c: MELAKA: A total of 79 candidates from various parties are contesting the 28 seats in the Melaka election, following the completion of the nomination process at all nomination centres across the state today.
This is a drop compared to the 112 candidates contesting in the 2021 state election.
Of the total candidates contesting in this year's Melaka polls, 24 candidates are representing Pakatan Harapan , followed by Barisan Nasional with 23, Bersama with 16 and Bersatu with seven.
Pas together with Parti Wawasan Negara and Gerakan are fielding candidates in five seats, three independents and one candidate from Parti Bumiputera Perkasa Malaysia (Putra).
Election Commission (EC) chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said no nomination papers were rejected.

"Eleven state constituencies would see straight fight while another 11 would see three-cornered contests. The remaining six constituencies would see four-cornered contests," he told reporters here today.
Of the 79 candidates, 65 are men and 14 are women.
He also said PH candidate for the Telok Mas seat Captain (Rtd) Mohamad Jaafar, 66, is the oldest candidate contesting the state election.
Ramlan said the youngest candidate is Muhammad Mukhlisul Mubin Julasapiyah, 24, also from PH, who is contesting the Kuala Linggi seat.
Mohamad is in a three-cornered contest for the Telok Mas seat against incumbent Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun of BN and Bersama's Muhammad Hazwan Mustafa.

Mukhlisul, also known as Mukhlis Mubin among his supporters, is contesting in a three-cornered fight in Kuala Linggi. He is up against incumbent Datuk Rosli Abdullah of BN and Datuk Ruzsyahriman Jenal of Bersama.
Ramlan said the campaign period began following the announcement of the candidates by the respective returning officers and would end at 11.59pm on Nov 13.
He also said EC has established 28 Election Campaign Enforcement Teams to monitor candidates' activities throughout the campaign period.

Ramlan said candidates who had paid the deposit for election campaign materials were subject to local authority by-laws governing the display and distribution of materials bearing their photographs, party emblems or symbols, as well as photographs of party leaders.
Permitted campaign materials include advertisements, leaflets, brochures, flags, banners, circulars, stickers, posters and temporary billboards.
Such materials must carry the names and addresses of their printers and publishers, except for flags, party symbol posters and photographs of party leaders or candidates.

Campaign materials containing seditious, racist or hateful words, or those touching on religious sensitivities in a way that could incite hostility, are prohibited and constitute an offence under the Election Offences Act 1954.
The EC also called on all parties to ensure that their campaign activities were conducted harmoniously and in compliance with the laws and regulations.
Ramlan said the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) had also set up an operations room that would operate round the clock from Oct 31 to Nov 14.
